diagnosis.summary: The nightly run abaa7ebb for 2026-10-01 failed at ingest because the customers landing file was never delivered. The other tables arrived intact, and customers delivered normally the day before, so this looks like a one-off delivery gap. I proposed a redelivery request for customers on 2026-10-01 only.

root_cause.explanation: landing/customers/dt=2026-10-01/customers.csv is absent, so ingest raised IngestError. Orders, order_items and payments for the same day are intact, and customers delivered normally on 2026-09-30 with a header that matched the contract.

evidence.claim: Ingest failed because the customers landing file for 2026-10-01 is missing.
The other three tables for 2026-10-01 arrived intact, and customers delivered normally on 2026-09-30. This is a one-off gap, not a format change.
The runbook says a missing landing file is fixed by upstream redelivery for the affected tables. It says redelivery is wrong for persistent schema or format changes.

alternatives_considered: rerun_only: rejected because the file is absent and a rerun alone would fail the same way.
Column mapping, parser or ignore-columns changes: rejected because there is no schema or format change, only a missing file.
Requesting redelivery for orders, order_items and payments too: rejected because those files arrived intact.
revert_model_change: rejected because the failure is at ingest and no dbt model is involved.
Escalating to upstream_app_team: held back unless redelivery returns no file. The source inspector only checked the contract path, so a misplaced file elsewhere is not ruled out.

proposal.rationale: The customers landing file for 2026-10-01 was never delivered (one-off gap). Customers delivered normally on 09-30 and the other three tables arrived intact on 10-01, so this is not a schema or format change. The runbook maps a missing landing file to upstream redelivery. Only customers is affected, so only customers is requested.
